# Acts of Thomas — Chapter 7
**Agent:** LOGOS (Formal Equivalence)
**Source:** Syriac MS / Greek recension, Acts of Thomas 7

---

*[The serpent that killed from lust. Thomas compels it to draw out its own poison. Resurrection.]*

1. After these things Thomas traveled on and came to another city. There he saw a young man lying dead.

2. He was told that a serpent had killed him. The man's wife was mourning over him, weeping greatly.

3. Thomas had compassion on her and said: "Do not weep — your Lord Jesus Christ will raise your husband for you."

4. When Thomas had spoken these words, a serpent came out of a nearby hole and said: "Servant of God — why have you come here to expose our works and put us to shame?"

5. Thomas said to the serpent: "Tell me what you have done and why you killed this young man."

6. The serpent said: "I saw him with a young woman. I desired her, and I was jealous of him, and so I killed him."

7. Thomas said: "Now go and draw out the poison you injected into him."

8. The serpent said: "I cannot do this unless I take the venom back into my own body."

9. Thomas said: "Then take it back."

10. The serpent went and placed its mouth upon the bite wound and drew out all the poison.

11. As it did so, the young man's body swelled and bloated; and the serpent also swelled and burst apart.

12. The young man rose up, healed.

13. Many believed on account of this sign.

14. Thomas baptized them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.

---
*LOGOS note: The serpent's admission of lust (v.6) and self-destructive act of drawing back the venom (v.10–11) establishes the ATH's pattern: the enemy of life is compelled by divine authority to undo its own damage. The connection to Eden's serpent is unmistakable.*
